source_trace: Qualifier run endpoint_scope performs real load_initializer/release before yield; authenticate_payloads authenticates training checkpoint and endpoint.pt then independently del disk/gc.collect/mapping_absent before reference. No source evidence shows it carries a live endpoint mmap into reference.

Copied loader fingerprint recursively walks tensors/container items with function-local closures and no persistent cache. Its input disk/buffers/overlay are mapped endpoint aliases during constructor. Clean successful constructor return discards its input frame; a failure frame can retain those aliases.

construct_encoder loads separate vision.pt, load_vision copies into existing model using strict default loading and removes hooks in finally; model buffers and absolute overlay use copy_. CheckpointPages owns scalar fd/range/advice metadata, not the tensor; copy explicitly calls value.to(device,copy=True) then consume. consume/release advise pages, not unmap or free tensor storage.

owned_copy reaches every Tensor in head/A/C/means/mu_train/common_statistics and preserves dict/list/tuple shape; each Tensor calls actual pages.copy. head_from allocates an independent residual head and strict-loads the already-owned tensors. Parameter A/C use copied storage. Processor/scope/provenance/encoder_identity/flags metadata use deepcopy. No successful-path direct disk tensor adoption is proven.

Processor cache is authenticated and required empty at constructor; no first-image forward occurred before failure. A dirty cache is possible only as a separate error path/owner question, not proven endpoint ownership. Actual shape/config/source/native runtime are untested here.

Copied load_inference deletes disk, gc.collects and runs exact mapping_absent before encoder_facts/return. The guard rejects mappings from ANY owner of the same device/inode, not only this invocation. Errors from functions holding mapped args can retain them via traceback; successful external owners can also trigger it.

reference_outputs catches, clears finished traceback frames across cause/context/groups, accumulates failures, then still runs release/after/registry cleanup. This occurs AFTER the loader mapping guard and cannot fix its earlier observation.

At final run raise_failures explicit native-exit group can suppress rendering of an earlier loader __context__; actual extracted raise_failures mechanism check confirms this. Printed absence of original exception neither proves nor disproves masking.

Installed runtime owned_copy/mapping_absent/apply_overlay/inference_readout_tree have exact copied-function AST equality. load_inference/construct_encoder follow the documented finite extraction substitutions; original failed before installed owner began.
